18683-ralph-granger-s-fortunes.title: Ralph Granger'S Fortunes
18683-ralph-granger-s-fortunes.creator: William Perry Brown
18683-ralph-granger-s-fortunes.description: A book by William Perry Brown. "This here was your father's gun. He carried it for many years. I had it when the feud betwixt the Grangers and the Vaughns first began. He had it with him when he was shot down at the Laurel Branch by John Vaughn, just six years ago today."

arxiv-2102-00359.title: Emergent route towards cooperation in interacting games: the dynamical reciprocity
arxiv-2102-00359.creator: Qin-Qin Wang, Ri-Zhou Liang, Ji-Qiang Zhang, Guo-Zhong Zheng, Lin Ma, Li Chen
arxiv-2102-00359.description: Abstract The success of modern civilization is built upon widespread cooperation in human society, deciphering the mechanisms behind has being a major goal for centuries. A crucial fact is, however, largely missing in most prior studies that games in the real world are typically played simultaneously and interactively rather than separately as assumed.

arxiv-2201-11252.title: Semantic Code Classification for Automated Machine Learning
arxiv-2201-11252.creator: Polina GusevaHSE University paguseva@edu.hse.ru Anastasia DrozdovaHSE University avdrozdova_2@edu.hse.ru Natalia DenisenkoHSE UniversityDaria SapozhnikovaHSE UniversityIvan PyaternevHSE UniversityAnna ScherbakovaHSE UniversityAndrey UstuzhaninHSE University
arxiv-2201-11252.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Polina GusevaHSE University paguseva@edu.hse.ru Anastasia DrozdovaHSE University avdrozdova_2@edu.hse.ru Natalia DenisenkoHSE UniversityDaria SapozhnikovaHSE UniversityIvan PyaternevHSE UniversityAnna ScherbakovaHSE UniversityAndrey UstuzhaninHSE University. A range of applications for automatic machine learning need the generation process to be controllable. In this work, we propose a way to control the output via a sequence of simple actions, that are called semantic code classes. Finally, we present a semantic code classification task and discuss methods for solving this problem on the Natural Language to Machine Learning (NL2ML) dataset.

arxiv-2202-13514.creator: Yunhao Du, Zhicheng Zhao, Yang Song
arxiv-2202-13514.description: Abstract Recently, multi-object tracking (MOT) has attracted increasing attention, and accordingly, remarkable progress has been achieved. However, the existing methods tend to use various basic models (e.g., detector and embedding models) and different training or inference tricks. As a result, the construction of a good baseline for a fair comparison is essential. In this paper, a classic tracker, i.e.

arxiv-2210-14705.title: Gradient flow of Einstein-Maxwell theory and Reissner-Nordström black holes
arxiv-2210-14705.creator: Davide De Biasio, Julian Freigang, Dieter Lüst, Toby Wiseman
arxiv-2210-14705.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Davide De Biasio, Julian Freigang, Dieter Lüst, Toby Wiseman. Ricci flow is a natural gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action. Here we consider the analog for the Einstein-Maxwell action, which gives Ricci flow with a stress tensor contribution coupled to a Yang-Mills flow for the Maxwell field. We argue that this flow is well-posed for static spacetimes with pure electric or magnetic potentialsand show it preserves both non-extremal and extremal black hole horizons.

arxiv-2212-05833.title: Measurement of the C ​ P CP properties of Higgs boson interactions with τ \tau -leptons with the ATLAS detector Journal: EPJC
arxiv-2212-05833.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2212-05833.description: Abstract A study of the charge conjugation and parity ( C ​ P CP ) properties of the interaction between the Higgs boson and τ \tau -leptons is presented. The study is based on a measurement of C ​ P CP -sensitive angular observables defined by the visible decay products of τ \tau -leptons produced in Higgs boson decays.

arxiv-2309-05090.title: Sculpting Efficiency: Pruning Medical Imaging Models for On-Device Inference
arxiv-2309-05090.creator: Sudarshan Sreeram, Bernhard Kainz
arxiv-2309-05090.description: Abstract Leveraging ML advancements to augment healthcare systems can improve patient outcomes. Yet, uninformed engineering decisions in early-stage research inadvertently hinder the feasibility of such solutions for high-throughput, on-device inference, particularly in settings involving legacy hardware and multi-modal gigapixel images.

arxiv-2310-14421.title: On existence, uniqueness and scalability of adversarial robustness and control measures for AI classifiers
arxiv-2310-14421.creator: Illia Horenko
arxiv-2310-14421.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Illia Horenko. Simply-verifiable mathematical conditions for existence, uniqueness and explicit analytical computation of minimal adversarial paths (MAP) and minimal adversarial distances (MAD) for (locally) uniquely-invertible classifiers, for generalized linear models (GLM), and for entropic AI (EAI) are formulated and proven.

arxiv-2401-02023.title: On Complexity of Stability Analysis in Higher-order Ecological Networks through Tensor Decompositions
arxiv-2401-02023.creator: Anqi Dong, Can Chen
arxiv-2401-02023.description: Abstract Complex ecological networks are often characterized by intricate interactions that extend beyond pairwise relationships. Understanding the stability of higher-order ecological networks is salient for species coexistence, biodiversity, and community persistence. In this article, we present complexity analyses for determining the linear stability of higher-order ecological networks through tensor decompositions.

arxiv-2402-10359.title: Can we soft prompt LLMs for graph learning tasks? Conference: The Web Conference 2024; May 13 - 17, 2024; Singapore
arxiv-2402-10359.creator: Zheyuan Liu, Xiaoxin He, Yijun Tian, Nitesh V. Chawla
arxiv-2402-10359.description: Abstract . Graph plays an important role in representing complex relationships in real-world applications such as social networks, biological data and citation networks. In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved tremendous success in various domains, which makes applying LLMs to graphs particularly appealing.

arxiv-2409-13128.title: Fast and Numerically Stable Implementation of Rate Constant Matrix Contraction Method
arxiv-2409-13128.creator: Shinichi Hemmi, Satoru Iwata, Taihei Oki
arxiv-2409-13128.description: Abstract The rate constant matrix contraction (RCMC) method, proposed by Sumiya et al. (2015, 2017), enables fast and numerically stable simulations of chemical kinetics on large-scale reaction path networks. Later, Iwata et al. (2023) mathematically reformulated the RCMC method as a numerical algorithm to solve master equations whose coefficient matrices, known as rate constant matrices, possess the detailed balance property.

arxiv-2412-18143.title: In charge for publications:
arxiv-2412-18143.creator: Rosane Teles Lins Castilho
arxiv-2412-18143.description: Abstract Monografias em Ciência da Computação, No. XX/AA ISSN: 0103-9741 Editor: Prof. Carlos José Pereira de Lucena Mes por extenso, AAAA NoSQL Graph Databases: an overview Veronica Santos, Bruno Cuconato Departamento de Informática, PUC-Rio {vdsantos, bclaro}@inf.puc-rio.br Abstract. Graphs are the most suitable structures for modeling objects and interactions in applications where component inter-connectivity is a key feature.

arxiv-2507-09757.title: Energy Dissipation Rate Guided Adaptive Sampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Resolving Surface-Bulk Dynamics in Allen-Cahn Systems
arxiv-2507-09757.creator: Chunyan Li, Wenkai Yu, Qi Wang
arxiv-2507-09757.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chunyan Li, Wenkai Yu, Qi Wang. We introduce the Energy Dissipation Rate guided Adaptive Sampling (EDRAS) strategy, a novel method that substantially enhances the performance of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) in solving thermodynamically consistent partial differential equations (PDEs) over arbitrary domains. EDRAS leverages the local energy dissipation rate density as a guiding metric to identify and adaptively re-sample critical collocation points from both the interior and boundary of the computational domain.

arxiv-2508-13393.title: Next-generation soliton frequency combs in photonic-crystal and nanocomposite microresonators Journal: opticajournal
arxiv-2508-13393.creator: Haixin Liu, Alexa Carollo, Jizhao Zang, Scott B. Papp
arxiv-2508-13393.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Haixin Liu, Alexa Carollo, Jizhao Zang, Scott B. Papp. Microresonator frequency combs offer tremendous opportunity to advance applications in fundamental research and technology by linking the optical and microwave frequency domains. Kerr-nonlinear microresonators further enable the generation of portable, integrated optical frequency combs, which are called microcombs. However, the dispersion engineering usually suffers from the small, geometric parameter space, and achieving soliton microcombs is challenging and usually requires complicated experimental techniques and setups.

arxiv-2510-08484.title: Guess your neighbor’s input: Quantum advantage in Feige’s game
arxiv-2510-08484.creator: Simon Schmidt, Sigurd A. L. Storgaard, Michael Walter, Yuming Zhao
arxiv-2510-08484.description: Abstract . In this article, we study a nonlocal game with two questions and three answers per player, which was first considered by Feige in 1991, and show that there is quantum advantage in this game. We prove that the game is a robust self-test for the 3 3 -dimensional maximally entangled state.

arxiv-2601-17074.title: PhysE-Inv: A Physics-Encoded Inverse Modeling approach for Arctic Snow Depth Prediction
arxiv-2601-17074.creator: Akila Sampath, Vandana Janeja & Jianwu Wang Department of Information Systems, UMBC {asampath, vjaneja, jianwu}@umbc.edu
arxiv-2601-17074.description: Abstract The accurate estimation of Arctic snow depth ( h s h_{s} ) remains a critical time-varying inverse problem due to the extreme scarcity and noise inherent in associated sea ice parameters. Existing process-based and data-driven models are either highly sensitive to sparse data or lack the physical interpretability required for climate-critical applications.

plos-pone-0354271.title: Long-term care hospitals as end-of-life care settings in South Korea: A nationwide analysis of utilization patterns and clinical trajectories
plos-pone-0354271.creator: Haein Kim, Seungwon Shin
plos-pone-0354271.description: Long-term care hospitals as end-of-life care settings in South Korea: A nationwide analysis of utilization patterns and clinical trajectories

pmc-10571416.title: Patient’s experiences of diabetes care at a tertiary health facility in Lilongwe, Malawi
pmc-10571416.creator: Ellen Nkambule, Kondwani Wella, Annie Msosa, Balwani Chingatichifwe Mbakaya, Evelyn Chilemba, Gladys Msiska
pmc-10571416.description: BackgroundLittle is known about experiences of rural people with diabetes care at a tertiary health facility in low-income settings. Understanding their experiences is essential for developing effective diabetes care interventions.MethodsThe study employed a qualitative narrative inquiry. Participants were identified at a diabetes clinic at a tertiary-level healthcare facility.

pmc-11308679.title: Pneumomediastinum and pneumoretroperitoneum after COVID-19: concealed intestinal perforation
pmc-11308679.creator: Jiaying Shen, Xiaoyong Shen, Feimin Zhao, Jianping Yao
pmc-11308679.description: BackgroundWith the prevalence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), many severe cases have been discovered worldwide. Here, a case of concurrent pneumomediastinum, pneumoretroperitoneum, and intestinal perforation was reported. This case was the first report on COVID-19-induced related complications.Case presentationA 74-year-old female patient was hospitalized for COVID-19. Air leakage was unexpectedly found during imaging reexamination.

pmc-11407693.title: High stakes slow responding, but do not help overcome Pavlovian biases in humans
pmc-11407693.creator: Johannes Algermissen, Hanneke E.M. den Ouden
pmc-11407693.description: “Pavlovian” or “motivational” biases are the phenomenon that the valence of prospective outcomes modulates action invigoration: the prospect of reward invigorates actions, while the prospect of punishment suppresses actions. Effects of the valence of prospective outcomes are well established, but it remains unclear how the magnitude of outcomes (“stake magnitude”) modulates these biases.

pmc-11418033.title: A rare case of central nervous system pancreatoblastoma metastasis: illustrative case
pmc-11418033.creator: Vincenzo Mastropasqua, Marco Obersnel, Vito Stifano, Marco Gessi, Domenico Cristiano Corsi, Francesco Doglietto
pmc-11418033.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BACKGROUNDPancreatoblastoma is a malignant neoplasm of the pancreas, occurring usually in children and rarely in adults. Treatment consists of surgery with a variable combination of adjuvant therapies. Liver metastases are common, whereas brain diffusion is exceptionally rare.OBSERVATIONSThe authors report the case of a 42-year-old man with a 16-year history of metastatic pancreatoblastoma, previously treated with surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, demonstrating a partial response. He presented with headache and dizziness, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a cerebellar lesion.

pmc-11442034.title: Case Study: Analyzing CFTR Mutations and SNPs in Pulmonary Fibrosis Patients with Unclear Symptoms
pmc-11442034.creator: Sahar Yousaf, Sumaira, Iqbal Bano, Atia Rehman, Samra Kousar, Muhammad Usman Ghani, Mariam Shahid
pmc-11442034.description: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a genetic monogenic disorder inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, marked by persistent airway infections in the endobronchial region. This condition leads to the gradual development of bronchiectasis and, ultimately, respiratory failure, emerging as the primary cause of mortality in individuals diagnosed with CF.

pmc-11466735.title: Investigation of the impact of multi-strain probiotics containing Saccharomyces cerevisiae on porcine production
pmc-11466735.creator: Sheena Kim, Jinho Cho, Gi Beom Keum, Jinok Kwak, Hyunok Doo, Yejin Choi, Juyoun Kang, Haram Kim, Yeongjae Chae, Eun Sol Kim, Minho Song, Hyeun Bum Kim
pmc-11466735.description: A balanced intestinal microbiome controls intestinal bacterial diseases, helps regulate immunity, and digests and utilizes nutrients, ultimately having a positive effect on the productivity of industrial animals. Yeasts help in the digestion process by breaking down indigestible fibers and producing organic acids, vitamins, and minerals.

pmc-11487495.title: Microfluidic Laser-Induced Nucleation of Iron (II,III) Oxide Nanoparticle-Doped Supersaturated Aqueous KCl Solutions
pmc-11487495.creator: Kelechi
pmc-11487495.description: A capillary-based microfluidic system designed for nonphotochemical laser-induced nucleation (NPLIN) studies coupled with real-time microscopy was used to study NPLIN of iron (II,III) oxide doped aqueous KCl solutions. Supersaturation was achieved by lowering the solution temperature using thermoelectric cooling, and heating was used for the dissolution of crystals downstream to prevent clogging during the flow.

pmc-12799551.title: Effectiveness of remineralizing dentifrices against caries lesions: A systematic approach
pmc-12799551.creator: Fatima T Zahra, Mehmood Asghar, Muhammad S Zafar, Asma T Shah, Muhammad Kaleem
pmc-12799551.description: ObjectivesDental caries remains a prevalent global oral health problem. Fluoride promotes enamel remineralization but is less effective on deeper lesions. Non-invasive agents, including bioactive glass and casein phosphopeptide-amorphous calcium phosphate (CPP-ACP), aim to enhance remineralization and prevent caries.MethodsA systematic review of in vitro studies was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

pmc-12872566.title: Association between sleep apnea-specific novel hypoxic metrics and disturbances in glucose and lipid metabolism
pmc-12872566.creator: Yujiao Zhang, Jiaqi Cai, Meirong Liu, Yan Wang, Haiyan Zhao, Jing Zhang
pmc-12872566.description: ObjectiveObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been linked to disturbances in glucose and lipid metabolism. The independent association between sleep apnea–specific novel hypoxic metrics and metabolic dysregulation in OSA, however, remains unclear.MethodsAnthropometric and polysomnographic data were obtained from OSA patients treated.

pmc-12971832.title: Working memory load and search efficiency in conventional monitor-based 2D versus 3D virtual settings: analysis of response times and parietal induced alpha activity in a modified Sternberg task
pmc-12971832.creator: Merle Sagehorn, Marike Johnsdorf, Joanna Kisker, Thomas Gruber, Benjamin Schöne
pmc-12971832.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In psychophysiological research on memory encoding and retrieval, Virtual Reality (VR) allows for meaningful insights into mnemonic processing under realistic conditions, yet its effects on working memory (WM) processing and performance remain inconclusive. The present study investigates how information search processes in WM differ when stimulus material is encoded in a conventional monitor-based context or in a more realistic virtual setting, and whether complex, naturalistic stimulus properties facilitate or challenge WM processing and task performance.

pmc-13093971.title: Psychometric validation of the Polish version of the Utrecht Gender Dysphoria Scale - Gender Spectrum questionnaire
pmc-13093971.creator: Agata Tokarek, Aleksandra Koczut, Agata Gasiorowska
pmc-13093971.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAccessible and inclusive tools for assessing gender dysphoria in Polish-speaking populations remain limited. To bridge this gap in care, there is an urgent need for accessible, psychometrically sound tools to assess Polish gender-diverse individuals.

pmc-13154083.title: Reversible Left Ventricular Hypertrabeculation and Hypermetabolism Following Bentall Procedure
pmc-13154083.creator: Kosuke Saku, Nobuhiro Tahara, Akihiro Honda, Shuichi Tanoue, Hiroyuki Otsuka, Satoru Tobinaga, Hiroyuki Tanaka, Yoshihiro Fukumoto, Eiki Tayama
pmc-13154083.description: BackgroundLeft ventricular hypertrabeculation may develop secondary to hemodynamic stress rather than represent primary cardiomyopathy. Its metabolic profile remains incompletely understood.Case SummaryA 43-year-old woman presented with heart failure secondary to severe aortic regurgitation from aortic root dilatation. Imaging demonstrated left ventricular dilation, reduced ejection fraction (39.0%), and prominent hypertrabeculation.

pmc-13233625.title: Enamel nanocrystal misorientation increased with meat-eating and agriculture
pmc-13233625.creator: Pupa U P A Gilbert, Daniel R Green, Patrick Mahoney, Debbie Guatelli-Steinberg, W Scott McGraw, Emma Lagan, Fredrick Kyalo Manthi, Samuel Muteti, Emmanuel Ndiema, Fernando Ramirez Rozzi, Cayla A Stifler, Connor A Schmidt, Barat Q Achinuq, Andreas Scholl, Benjamin Gilbert, Mackie C O’Hara
pmc-13233625.description: Enamel covers teeth, is the hardest tissue in the vertebrate body and has a complex multiscale structure from nanometres to millimetres1. The structure comprises thin, long hydroxyapatite (Ca5(PO4)3OH) nanocrystals2, 50–70 nm wide, many micrometres long, parallel and bundled into approximately 5-µm-wide rods. The rods undulate and cross into a microscale ‘decussation pattern’ that toughens enamel by deflecting cracks3,4.

pmc-13315895.title: Andes Virus on a Cruise Ship, what it Tells us About the Global Pandemic Preparedness Agenda
pmc-13315895.creator: Marion Koopmans, Christian Brechot, Roberto Bruzzone, Moussa Moïse Diagne, Christian Drosten, Isabella Eckerle, Robert Gallo, David T.S. Hayman, Peter Horby, Peter Hotez, Menno de Jong, Florian Krammer, Jean Claude Manuguerra, Gustavo Palacios, Massimo Palmarini, Anja Schreijer, Nicole D. Tischler,
pmc-13315895.description: SummaryThe outbreak of hantavirus disease caused by Andes virus aboard a cruise ship is a reminder of the challenges posed by emerging diseases in the modern era. While Andes virus-associated disease can be particularly severe, it is unlikely to spread extensively beyond the current number of cases or emerge as a large epidemic, especially if public health measures are followed.

pmc-13378331.title: Luteinizing hormone change trajectories in gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonist protocols are associated with assisted reproductive outcomes: results from a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13378331.creator: Xun Su, Qi Zheng, Dongyang Zhang, Qian Li, Hua Zhang, Yiqing Fan, Tao Yin, Weiwei Zou, Lei Zhang, Jie Zhang, Zhaolian Wei, Yunxia Cao, Chunmei Liang, Dongmei Ji
pmc-13378331.description: ContextLuteinizing hormone (LH) plays an integral role in follicular development. In gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist protocols, LH levels have been demonstrated to affect assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes. However, the exact nature of this relationship remains unclear, and LH measurements at a single time point may not be sufficient to capture it fully.

pmc-13654392.title: Balloon-Expandable Vs Self-Expanding Valves for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Internally Stented Surgical Valves
pmc-13654392.creator: Daisuke Sato, Noriaki Moriyama, Yoichi Sugiyama, Hirokazu Miyashita, Tomoki Ochiai, Koki Shishido, Futoshi Yamanaka, Tommi Vähäsilta, Teemu Laakso, Sebastian Dahlbacka, Tiina Vainikka, Juho Viikilä, Shigeru Saito, Mika Laine, Mikko Jalanko
pmc-13654392.description: BackgroundInternally stented (IS) surgical valves, such as Mitroflow (Sorin Group, Arvada, CO) and Trifecta (St. Jude Medical), are known to carry an elevated risk for coronary artery obstruction during valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures. The data from comparison between balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and supra-annular self-expanding valves (SEVs) for ViV-TAVI within the IS valve remains unclear.

uslaw-usc-t10-s7726.title: 10 U.S.C. § 7726 — Oversight and inspections
uslaw-usc-t10-s7726.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7726.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (Service, Supply, And Procurement); Chapter 776 (Army National Military Cemeteries). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Inspections Required.— The Secretary of the Army shall provide for the oversight of the Cemeteries to ensure the highest quality standards are maintained by providing for the periodic inspection of the administration, operation and maintenance, and construction.
